ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of founder, UBO, and resident agent against Panama UAF risk indicators, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions, Interpol red notices, and domestic maritime/commercial sanctions lists; enhanced due diligence required for any PEP exposure; automated dropshipping using Stripe/PayPal classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced with ongoing transaction monitoring and quarterly adverse-media screening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registros, Sistema de Reserva de Nombre (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official corporate language; all legal names must be rendered in Latin script, with standard Spanish diacritics permitted but discouraged for clearinghouse processing; non-Spanish names must be transliterated to the roman alphabet; the name must include the statutory expression 'Private Interest Foundation', 'Fundación de Interés Privado', or equivalent clearly recognized by the Public Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File one extension request for an additional 30 days before expiration; a rejected name may be cured by correcting prohibited tokens and re-filing. Where the Public Registry issues a final rejection, submit a written 'Recurso de Apelación' to the Dirección General de Registro within 5 business days, annexing the rejection notice and a revised name certificate; after exhaustion, pursue administrative-judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Private Interest Foundation must maintain a permanent registered office in Panama at the physical office of its licensed resident agent. A virtual office may be used solely as the registered address where it corresponds to the resident agent's street address and business premises; a P.O. Box alone is not permissible. No substantive commercial presence, employees, or physical stock is required for an automated dropshipping operation, though a separate operating company is recommended to ring-fence merchant payment-account liability.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 12% annual likelihood of an unannounced inspection for a passive medium-risk PIF used solely for dropshipping; risk increases to around 30% if the foundation directly holds wire-transfer merchant funds, exceeds the UAF reporting thresholds, or uses high-risk payment rails without dedicated operating company segregation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley 32 de 2011; Articles 6 (minimum endowment), 7-11 (foundation charter and registration), and 24-27 (Foundation Council and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Private Interest Foundations Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública Constitutiva / Acta Fundacional) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial endowment of US$10,000 (or equivalent) under Article 6 of Law 25 of 1995; the endowment must be declared subscribed and fully paid in the Foundation Charter. No escrow account is legally required; a notarized sworn declaration of contribution suffices.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the Foundation's initial endowment of US$10,000 is duly subscribed, allocated, and declared fully paid; (2) that the statutory registered office is established at the address of the Resident Agent in the Republic of Panama, and such Agent is formally appointed; (3) that the following officers are appointed: President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the Foundation Council; any two officers acting jointly may open, operate, and close bank accounts and sign resolutions; (4) that the Foundation adopts its internal regulations, consistent with anti-money-laundering and tax information obligations; and (5) that the officers are authorized to execute and file all ancillary documents necessary to finalize incorporation, including tax registration and any municipal filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter containing the foundation name, automated dropshipping purpose (retail sale via automated e-commerce networks), endowment declaration of US$10,000, names of Foundation Council members, resident agent acceptance, and registered office. Formalize execution in the presence of a notary; obtain notarized first and second copies (testimonios).
required_dossiers: Passport copies and address proof of the founder and council members
Resident Agent acceptance and registered office confirmation
Sworn capitalization declaration of initial endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries identity or capacity, correct the underlying documents and re-execute the charter before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and inscription with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) – Private Interest Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Foundation Charter together with the Registry fee payment; the Registry examiner verifies the endowment and charter form and assigns a registration number when the foundation is inscribed in the Foundations Register.
required_dossiers: Original notarized copy of the Escritura Pública Constitutiva
Registry application cover sheet (solicitud de inscripción)
Receipt of official state filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a query (reparo), file a written response and proposed corrective clause within the statutory period; resubmit an amended charter if the defect is substantive.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of certified registration certificate and registered charter copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Certification and Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, request the certified foundation registration certificate and a certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter; verify the exact foundation name, registration date, and Foundation Council composition against the Registry record.
required_dossiers: Applicant identification using the foundation registration reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certified copy contains discrepancies, request re-certification or coordinate a rectification note through the Registry's rectification procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax identification registration (RUC) and municipal operating notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; Municipality of Panama (Tesorería Municipal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Foundation for Panamanian tax identification (RUC) and, if the Foundation executes any local activity, file the Aviso de Operación with the Municipality. Maintain the RUC and fiscal compliance registry updated with the Foundation's address.
required_dossiers: Certified Foundation Charter and registration certificate
Foundation Council resolution appointing legal representative for tax matters
Passport or ID copies of founder and appointed representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or municipal window highlights discrepancies, align the charter and resolution data (names, addresses) with the registry record and resubmit the complete file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of officers and adoption of corporate governance minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council and internal foundation secretary; optional officer appointment note at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Foundation Council to adopt the First Board Resolution, appoint President, Treasurer and Secretary, adopt internal regulations, acknowledge the registered office, and authorize officers to finalize bank account opening and money-laundering prevention compliance. Record the resolution in the minutes book and deliver certified copies to officers.
required_dossiers: Council acceptance instruments for President, Treasurer and Secretary
Internal anti-money-laundering manual and KYC file of the founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer appointment document is rejected by an external institution, re-convene the Council to ratify a curative resolution confirming the appointment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – automated dropshipping operations require no Panamanian industrial or manufacturing license
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no physical license required for the automated dropshipping business model

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente – MiAMBIENTE), National Directorate of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – automated dropshipping has no physical infrastructure or environmental footprint in Panama
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – zero local wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or regulated waste generation arising from the dropshipping activity

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – the Foundation maintains no physical premises, warehouses, or workplace in Panama; fire-safety certification and structural load inspections will be triggered solely upon establishment of any future physical office or storage facility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); electronic portal: SICE (Sistema Informático de Cobro Electrónico) — includes the RUC registry, electronic invoicing module (E-Factura / Facturación Electrónica), and online filing (declaraciones); customs interface coordinated with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) and its SICE-SADEX export declaration module.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) established under Law 25 of 1995 must first complete its registration at the Registro Público de Panamá (public deeds registry) with a duly appointed Registered Agent and Council (Consejo de la Fundación). If the PIF engages in any activity with Panamanian tax nexus, it must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) by submitting Form RUC (Formulario de Inscripción), certified copy of the foundation charter and its public registry inscription, identity documentation of the Registered Agent and Councillors, proof of fiscal domicile in Panama, and appointment of a local CPA (Contador Público Autorizado) where accounting records are kept in Panama. Filing is performed online through the SICE portal or physically at DGI kolektoría offices; DGI issues the RUC certificate and activates the taxpayer's digital certificate (Firma Electrónica) enabling e-invoicing and electronic filing. A PIF conducting purely offshore dropshipping transactions (no Panama-source sales, no Panamanian employees, no local registered establishment) is not legally obliged to hold a RUC, but obtaining a voluntary RUC is the established practice for bank due diligence, platform merchant verification (Stripe/PayPal), and documentary proof of the territorial tax exclusion.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — Panama applies a strict territorial income tax system (Código Fiscal Art. 694): income, assets, and transfers sourced outside Panama are excluded from Panamanian taxation. A PIF is a separate legal person, not a pass-through, but its foreign-source dropshipping commissions and gains are exempt from Panamanian income tax under Law 25 of 1995; the PIF is not a resident taxpayer for income tax purposes unless it develops a permanent establishment or derives Panama-source income (e.g., sales to Panamanian consumers, local fulfillment in Panama, local storage, or invoicing through a Panamanian branch). In that case it becomes an ordinary territorial taxpayer subject to 25% corporate income tax on Panama-source net income. The PIF is not eligible for 'tax-exempt zone' treatment (Colón Free Zone / Ciudad del Saber regime) unless physically established inside such zones.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists in Panama's domestic law. Available elections include: (i) voluntary registration with the RUC to document the territorial exclusion; (ii) election by the PIF's Council to conduct business through a Panamanian fiscal representative/agent for DGI compliance; (iii) election to qualify as a small taxpayer (Régimen Simplificado del Pequeño Contribuyente) where annual gross turnover does not exceed PAB 36,000; (iv) election to apply the export incentive regime for physical exports from Panama (e.g., re-export schemes using Zona Libre de Colón or the SEM regime) with the DGI registration of the exporter; (v) such electoral choices in the foundation bylaws as govern the distribution of taxable vs. non-taxable patrimony. Panama has not adopted OECD hybrid mismatch rules; Law 254 of 2021 (Economic Substance and BEPS-aligned transparency) merely imposes economic substance documentation and reporting obligations, not substitution of the PIF's legal identity or a check-the-box classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – a national VAT-type tax governed by Articles 1050–1092 of the Código Fiscal, as amended by Laws 8 of 2010, 38 of 2017 and 365 of 2023; complements the mandatory electronic invoicing regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB 0.00 — no general de minimis turnover threshold: any person, including a non-resident foreign entity or PIF, that habitually carries out taxable transfers of goods or renders services within Panamanian territory is required to register for ITBMS and file monthly returns, regardless of volume. An optional simplified small-taxpayer regime (Régimen Simplificado del Pequeño Contribuyente) applies to taxable persons with annual gross income up to PAB 36,000 and provides a reduced compliance burden; however, this regime does not exempt a foreign e-commerce seller from the obligation to register where a Panamanian nexus (local customer base, Panamanian warehouse, or local platform account) exists. A purely automated offshore dropshipping operation with no Panamanian nexus falls outside the scope of ITBMS altogether. The standard registration threshold is therefore PAB 0.00; the operational threshold is PAB 36,000 only for the optional simplified regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing applies progressively to all RUC holders: taxpayers issue e-invoices through DGI-certified software or the free SICE web portal; each fiscal document requires real-time electronic authorization (Código de Autorización) generated by the DGI central validation gateway before the document is legally effective, with full JSON/XML schema validation, digital signature stamping, and archiving in the DGI's SICE repository. DGI Resolution 201-1665 of 2019, Resolution DGI 201-2880 of 2020, and successive resolutions govern the API integration requirements, the card-not-present payment certification, and the mandatory acceptance of e-invoices for ITBMS credit, export zero-rating, and customs formalities. Non-Ecuadorian foreign dropshipping merchants without a Panamanian establishment are not subject to the e-invoicing mandate; if, however, the PIF holds a voluntary RUC or conducts any Panama-source transfer, e-invoicing and real-time clearance are unconditionally mandatory even for the zero-rated export transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Panama are zero-rated for ITBMS provided the exporter is a registered ITBMS taxpayer, the goods leave Panama under a customs export declaration processed by ANA, and the foreign currency proceeds are received by the exporter; the zero-rated treatment is evidenced on the e-invoice with the ITBMS 0% rate. Cross-border services rendered from Panama to non-resident beneficiaries (including digital distribution, software, and logistics services) are zero-rated where the services are effectively used or exploited outside Panama. For pure automated dropshipping in which goods flow directly from an offshore supplier to an offshore end-customer and the PIF only collects margins through Stripe/PayPal, no ITBMS is triggered because the transfer does not occur in Panamanian territory; zero-rating is only relevant (and available) when the goods physically transit through Panama, in which case the exporter must duly register, file the SICE-SADEX export declaration, and retain proof of export and payment. The PIF cannot reclaim ITBMS credits on purchases unrelated to a Panamanian taxable activity; refund claims are limited to excess input credits arising from Panama-source zero-rated exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación via SICE-SADEX / ANA VED system)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical departure from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or bank/PSP settlement statement proving receipt of export proceeds
Commercial Invoice / Packing List issued by the PIF (or its agent) and matching the customs value
E-Invoice (Factura Electrónica) with ITBMS 0% rate and DGI authorization code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA jointly verify export transactions, cross-checking customs declarations, e-invoices, freight documents, and bank remittances. If the exporter fails to repatriate the invoiced foreign currency through the national banking system within 180 calendar days from the date of shipment (or obtains a timely extension from DGI), the transaction is retrospectively reclassified as a domestic taxable transfer: the exporter is assessed the 7% ITBMS, plus monthly surcharge of 10% on arrears (maximum 100% of the tax), adjusted interest, and fines provided under Articles 712, 719, 729 and related provisions of the Código Fiscal. Fraudulent export substantiation (false customs declarations, fabricated bills of lading, fictitious inward remittance certificates, or artificially staged re-export arrangements) triggers immediate revocation of the exporter status, clawback of the ITBMS exemption for up to the full prescription period (generally five fiscal years), monetary penalties from PAB 500 to PAB 5,000, and criminal tax fraud liability carrying imprisonment of up to five years. Where the DGI proves that the PIF existed solely to obtain the export zero-rating benefit, the territorial protection of Law 25 of 1995 is disregarded under the general anti-abuse powers introduced by Law 254 of 2021, subjecting the underlying economic activity to standard territorial ITBMS and income tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of Panama does not maintain a traditional central bank; full dollarization (USD legal tender) provides monetary stability. Banking examination, AML/CFT oversight, licensing, and compliance enforcement are vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). Fiscal agency and treasury-clearing functions are performed by Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama). No separate foreign-exchange administration exists; the Ministry of Economy and Finance sets no exchange-control policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates under full de jure and de facto capital and current account convertibility. The US dollar circulates as the exclusive paper legal tender, while the balboa exists solely as a fractional coin at a fixed 1:1 parity. There are no exchange-control laws, no repatriation restrictions, no currency surrender obligations, and no prior Central Bank authorization for cross-border fund movements. Profit remittances by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) to non-resident council members or beneficiaries are freely permitted; Panama's territorial tax system imposes tax only on Panama-source income, and outbound remittances of previously untaxed offshore earnings are not subject to withholding or exchange approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender rules exist in Panama. Exporters and digital-commerce intermediaries are not required to convert export receipts into local currency (there is no managed exchange rate), nor to remit proceeds to a nationalized account within a fixed timeline. All proceeds derived by a PIF from automated dropshipping networks may be retained in USD domiciled abroad or in Panama with no repatriation obligation. Compliance focuses instead on documentary support of the underlying commercial transactions under SBP AML/CFT Regulation and FATF-aligned beneficial ownership standards.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with E-Banking Treasury Module
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM with conservative legal engineering. Panama does not maintain a standalone Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime comparable to UK/Pillar EBA; non-bank payment services generally require SBP authorization under the Panama Payment System Law (Ley 99 de 2020) and adherence to SBP AML/CFT Rule 2028. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK FCA-authorised, Lithuania-licensed) may service a Panama PIF but must not establish a physical branch in Panama without a banking or payment-service license; the foundation should structure treasury flows directly to a correspondent USD account in Panama and avoid having an unlicensed EMI act as a UI-collection gateway for Stripe/PayPal settlement if those flows would amount to a regulated payment business onshore. Legal constraint: PIF bank account title must reflect the foundation's full name (Foundation Name, Private Interest Foundation); use of an unlicensed intermediary for payment routing materially elevates AML risk and may trigger SBP Article 27 reporting obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: SBP Regulation 2015-19 and subsequent DAC-2021 guidance permit client onboarding without mandatory physical appearance only when the bank applies enhanced video-identification procedures, independent third-party data verification, and a final risk-based interview conducted by the Compliance Officer. In practice, most Panama Tier-1 commercial banks require at least one of the PIF's registered agents, foundation council members, or beneficial owners to attend an in-person interview at the bank's Panama City premises (or at the Panamanian consulate abroad). Remote opening is legally permissible for low-risk structures but is rarely granted for a medium-risk automated dropshipping PIF with foreign settlor and nominee council members; the prudent blueprint mandates a designated director or fiduciary law-firm principal physically present for KG-signature, notarized foundation resolution, and face-to-face validation of the commercial model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement concentration on Stripe and PayPal with volatile transaction velocity (hundreds of micro-orders per day), elevated chargeback ratios, and multiple customer countries from a single U.S. dollar account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Upload to the bank's AML portal: (i) executed dropshipping master supplier contracts with each third-party fulfillment house; (ii) 6 months of platform settlement reports from Stripe and PayPal showing receivable aging and chargeback disputes; (iii) a signed compliance attestation confirming compliance with both Stripe Acceptable Use Policy and SBP Rule 2028; (iv) consumer order and refund policy; (v) a third-party transaction monitoring summary produced by the PIF's outsourced AML service provider; and (vi) logistics proof-of-delivery records (3070).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: PIF Law 25/1995 hybrid structure with settlor, council members, or protectors not appearing in any commercial registry or tax filing, creating a classic shell-structure red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarized foundation charter and foundation regulations; certificate from the Public Registry of Panama listing the foundation's qualified date; DGI Beneficial Owner Tax Information declaration (Form 812) demonstrating beneficial owner identification; written opinion from a Panamanian law firm confirming that the foundation's purpose is lawful cross-border e-commerce treasury management, not asset concealment; signed declaration of source of wealth with bank reference from the settlor's domestic bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire instructions from high-risk jurisdictions or receivable collection from forwarder/payment aggregators not matching the contracted supplier list, creating trade-based money-laundering indication.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive transaction ledger mapping each incoming payout (date, gross amount, platform fee, currency, originating bank/PSP) to matching invoices and proof-of-delivery events; contracts with all identified intermediaries; prior tax residency certificate or equivalent from the PIF's home jurisdiction; annual audited financial statements of the PIF; power-of-attorney register clearly stating the sole-approval authority for outbound disbursements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection to the PIF should be executed by SWIFT MT103 from the settlor's corporate or high-net-worth bank account to the PIF's Panamanian USD operational account at a Tier-1 bank. Recommended purpose code/remittance reference: 'CONTB / CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION PA_PIF' — Panama does not impose mandatory central bank purpose codes; however, include the standard ancillary code 'TRAK' for tracking, and avoid the code 'GIFT'. The initiating bank must complete robust verification protocols: match the sending legal name against the foundation charter, validate the beneficial ownership declaration, confirm the absence of sanctions and PEP hits, and in the event of an inbound of USD 100,000 or more, the receiving bank will apply SBP Rule 2028 enhanced EDD procedures. For Stripe/PayPal treasury buffers held outside Panama, injection of those funds into Panama should source from a single owned aggregator account to minimize fragmentation; each tranche must reference the platform payout report and be accompanied by a foundation council resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement for dropshipping supplies and logistics will be cleared over four priority rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 USD wire transfers for all supplier invoices exceeding USD 1,500 through the PIF's Panama-based USD account, relying on the Bank's U.S. Federal Reserve correspondent network (Fedwire and CHIPS); (2) commercial letters of credit issued under UCP 600 for high-value inventory procurement of more than USD 50,000, with the PIF as applicant and suppliers as beneficiaries, credited through advising banks in Hong Kong or Singapore; (3) Automated ACH/ACH-Same-Day rails for U.S. domestic fulfillment partners, executed via the Panama bank's correspondent ACH membership to the U.S. Automated Clearing House, limited to suppliers with established transaction history; (4) dedicated PSP settlement schedules with Stripe and PayPal using explicit payout triggers and minimum balance thresholds to prevent liquidity fragmentation. All outbound transfers shall include trading-related remittance details (invoice number, PO number, Incoterms) and be mirrored against the individual fulfillment invoice to satisfy SBP transaction monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CLS-settled USD/EUR spot and one-month to six-month offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) executed with a London or New York bank prudently not required for locking merchant settlement risk
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) between USD and EUR denominated balances with an SBP-licensed international bank's non-Panama affiliate (tenor up to 12 months)
Over-the-counter FX options (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) purchased to cap procurement liability in non-USD supplier invoices, margin-collateralized in USD
Offshore FX forward contracts used exclusively in hedge-accounting mode with documented underlying receivables/liabilities arising from automated dropshipping purchase orders
FX conversion at settlement time through the Tier-1 bank's treasury desk, expressly excluding leveraged or speculative structures prohibited under the PIF's constitutional documents

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tasa Única Anual — annual single fee declaration and payment for the Private Interest Foundation (Panama Foundation Annual Franchise Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, remitted through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 January of each calendar year; the pro-rated first payment for a newly incorporated foundation is settled at registration and the next Tasa Única falls due on 15 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus monthly default interest; DGI withholds the Paz y Salvo Fiscal required for amendments or dissolution; two consecutive unpaid years mark the foundation inactive and expose it to administrative strike-off by the Public Registry (Ley 13 de 2021)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership declaration and confirmation update (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales / UBO annual update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI beneficial-ownership electronic register maintained jointly with the Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 January, aligned to the Tasa Única calendar; any change in beneficiaries or Foundation Council membership must be reported within 15 business days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of USD 500–5,000 per breach against the foundation and/or its Resident Agent; the foundation is blocked from executing notarial or Public Registry filings until the register is rectified; repeated breaches may trigger Resident Agent resignation and consequential administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax declaration (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta) — conditionally required only when the foundation realizes Panamanian-source revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Tax Administration via the Panamanian e-tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the fiscal year end for calendar-year taxpayers (fiscal year ending 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing fine of USD 50–500 irrespective of tax due, default interest at 1% per month, and penalty surcharges up to 25% of any assessed Panamanian-source tax; foreign-source dropshipping revenue remains exempt under Panama's territorial tax regime

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Private Interest Foundation as such. Audit compulsion arises only when (i) the foundation is licensed or supervised by the banking, securities, or insurance regulators; (ii) the foundation holds Panamanian real estate or a Panamanian operating entity and the DGI requests audited financial statements during a tax audit; or (iii) audited accounts are contractually required by a financing counterparty. A remote automated-dropshipping foundation whose revenue is generated wholly through foreign payment rails and third-party fulfillment has no statutory audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted by Panama applies to statutory financial statements; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for small-scale entities; internal books may be maintained on a cash basis for offshore revenue tracking while coordinating with the Resident Agent and any external accountant.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council and the Resident Agent jointly confirm the identity of the settlor, Foundation Council members, protector, and beneficiaries in the DGI beneficial-ownership declaration each calendar year. Shareholding transfers are not applicable because the PIF has no capital stock; changes to the foundation's benefit structure are effected by a notarized deed of amendment (Acto de Enmienda) executed by the Foundation Council, filed in the Public Registry when real property is involved, and the private register of beneficial interests is updated at the registered office within 15 business days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Protector Appointments (Registro de Personas Beneficiarias) kept at the Resident Agent's office
Foundation Council Minutes Book (Libro de Actas) recording annual meetings and resolutions
Foundation Charter and Full Amendment Trail (Escritura Pública de Constitución and all registered amendments)
Accounting Records Ledger (Libros Contables) documenting underlying transactions for any prepared financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–1,200 per year for a standard Panama Resident Agent and registered-office package, including administration of the annual Tasa Única and UBO registry filings; market range varies by agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not mandated for a non-regulated PIF; voluntary IFRS audit budget of USD 1,500–4,000 for a low-volume e-commerce/dropshipping structure, or USD 600–1,500 for a compilation/review without an audit certificate

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies territorial taxation: Panamanian-source income is taxable at 25%, while foreign-source income derived by a Panama Private Interest Foundation from automated dropshipping networks is generally outside the Panamanian tax net. No broad statutory tax holidays apply to ordinary dropshipping activity; special regime exemptions (e.g., Colon Free Zone, Panama-Pacifico SEM, City of Knowledge) are not automatically available to an ISIC 4791 automated dropshipping structure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1372 (Declaración Anual de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed through the Sede Electrónica de la DGI (e-Tax portal at dgi.gob.pa). Electronic filing is mandatory for all active juridical persons.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending 31 December, the return is due no later than 31 March of the following year; for non-calendar fiscal years, the return is due within three months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC, legal name, registered address, registered agent, and ISIC 4791 activity code declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIF owners must ensure the Panama registered agent is correctly recorded and the activity code reflects automated dropshipping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts derived from Panamanian customers, Panamanian payment rails, or activities performed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue with Panamanian source; foreign dropshipping sales sourced outside Panama should not be included in taxable Panama-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts derived from foreign customers and foreign supply chains, reported for information and territorial exemption monitoring.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs may report foreign-source dropshipping revenue as tax-exempt, but must maintain documentary evidence of foreign order origin, payment routing, and supplier delivery terms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs, chargebacks, platform fees, payment processor fees, and logistics expenses attributable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs may claim deductions only against Panama-source income; expenses allocated to foreign-source revenue are not deductible against Panamanian tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 - Net Taxable Income and 25% Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions, calculated at the 25% corporate rate, reduced by advance payments and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF with exclusively foreign-source dropshipping income should report zero Panamanian-source taxable income and zero tax, but must still file the annual return while registered.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 1.5% on unpaid tax, default interest, and a late-filing penalty of 10% to 50% of the tax due. Repeated non-filing can lead to administrative closure, RUC suspension, and referral for criminal tax prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends paid or credited out of Panamanian-source taxable profits. Distributions from a PIF consisting of foreign-source dropshipping profits are not subject to Panamanian dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Panama double tax agreement, the beneficial owner must submit a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty counterparty, together with a DTA relief request and proof of beneficial ownership. The TRC must be current, apostilled or legalized, translated into Spanish if required, and filed through the DGI e-Tax portal or with the Panamanian withholding agent. Reduced withholding rates apply prospectively after DGI validation and generally require annual renewal.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on Panamanian-source royalties and non-banking interest paid to non-residents is 12.5% for each category; treaty rates typically range from 5% to 10% depending on the applicable DTA. Interest derived through Panama's international banking center may be exempt under specific statutory rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is required when annual related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000; Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds USD 50 million. A transfer pricing informative return must also be filed where related-party transactions meet the applicable threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not operate a standalone schedule of Economic Substance Regulations for PIFs in the offshore-holding context, but substance is tested through Panama's beneficial ownership registry under Law 254 of 2021, DGI anti-abuse examinations, and foreign DTA limitation-of-benefits clauses. A dropshipping PIF must demonstrate local registered agency, decision-making records, a Panama bank account, and real economic activity to defend territorial tax treatment and treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Misdeclared Source of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately mischaracterizing Panamanian-source dropshipping revenue as foreign-source income, understating gross receipts, or using the PIF to conceal sales to Panamanian consumers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of unpaid tax plus 100% surcharge, monthly recalculated interest, monetary fines, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud with imprisonment of up to 5 years or more for aggravated evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members who sign false returns may be jointly and severally liable for civil restitution; criminal conviction can trigger personal fines, travel restrictions during proceedings, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a pure paper structure with no local governance, no bank account, no commercial records, or with artificial interposition solely to avoid foreign tax on automated dropshipping profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may disregard the PIF's separate legal personality, recharacterize worldwide income as Panamanian-source, deny treaty benefits, impose 100% penalty on the omitted tax, and invalidate transactions with retroactive effect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil for fraud or abuse of the PIF's legal form, imposing direct restitution obligations on foundation council members and authorizing asset freezes and exit bans during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Stripe, PayPal, or other payment rails without maintaining beneficial ownership disclosure, customer KYC, source-of-funds records, or transaction monitoring, particularly with high-volume automated dropshipping flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under Panama's AML Law 23 of 2015 range from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 per violation, plus license suspension for payment intermediaries and criminal liability for money-laundering offenses with imprisonment from 5 to 12 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and authorized signatories can face personal criminal liability, civil confiscation of proceeds, travel bans, and imprisonment for knowingly structuring payments to avoid transparency thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated cost-of-goods-sold to a related supplier in a low-tax jurisdiction, underpricing dropshipping distribution services, or failing to prepare and file mandatory Local File, Master File, and informative TP returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may adjust the transaction to the arm's length price, assess the 25% corporate tax on the adjustment, add monthly surcharges and interest, and impose TP documentation penalties of up to 40% of the adjusted amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or fail to challenge non-arm's length related-party contracts may be held liable for restitution of the resulting tax deficiency and may be subject to criminal charges if the pricing scheme is found to be fraudulent.
